chapter: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
title: Earl Roberts, the Showboat and the Depression
summary: The manager from Massachusetts cannot find good jobs as the Depression sets in, and the band breaks up.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Why weren't you able to get any more jobs? Didn't you tell me that you were playing up in Albany when Roosevelt was elected and they had the inaugural parade, or something?
I don't remember anything about a parade.
Why weren't you able to get any more jobs?
We had a guy by the name of Earl Roberts--
That was the guy that owned the Showboat.
He had an interest in it. He was from Massachusetts. He got so that he booked us

right down into Oklahoma. He booked us down in Oklahoma, we played two nights at the Oklahoma Ballroom where we played before; we played long engagements. This is with Earl Roberts and he just couldn't get any more good jobs, couldn't get me any more good jobs and the Depression had started.
Didn't seem like there was any way you could continue.
Meyer Davis wanted us to go into the Arcadia Ballroom and (inaudible) was afraid that the band would break up. I know I had two, three offers to go to a band and I wouldn't pay them no mind.
